sub_criteria.name: agentic search design
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates an LLM-driven system that searches scholarly literature through more than one query: query reformulation, citation-graph traversal, iterative crawling, planning or tool use.

sub_criteria.name: baseline recall
sub_criteria.text: Reports what plain single-query or conventional keyword/dense database search recovers, as a measured baseline or ceiling that other systems are compared against.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Introduces or analyses an evaluation set for literature search, deep research or scholarly QA, and says how the set was built, annotated or scored.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval and reranking
sub_criteria.text: Contributes or evaluates the underlying retrieval or reranking method — dense/sparse retrieval, LLM rerankers, citation-graph or hybrid retrieval — on scientific documents.

sub_criteria.name: gains that fail
sub_criteria.text: Reports a failure to replicate, benchmark leakage or construction that inflates scores, a weak or unfairly tuned baseline, or a setting where the simple baseline is not beaten.

items.title: Deep Research Pretraining via Predictive Navigation
items.abstract_600: Deep research agents are often trained on expensive, environment-grounded tool-use trajectories that require repeated retrieval, document inspection, and report evaluation. We introduce Deep Research Pretraining (DRP), an offline framework that derives predictive navigation supervision from naturally occurring evidence structures. Given a citation-bearing or hyperlinked passage, DRP constructs a proxy research objective, recovers linked evidence and graph-related alternatives, and converts them into search-open-write trajectories. items.title: One Pass, Any Order: Position-Invariant Listwise Reranking for LLM-Based Recommendation
items.abstract_600: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for recommendation reranking, but their listwise predictions can depend on the order in which candidates are presented. This creates a mismatch between the set-based nature of recommendation and the sequence-based computation of decoder-only LLMs, where permuting an otherwise identical candidate set can change item scores and final rankings. Such order sensitivity makes LLM-based rerankers difficult to rely on, since rankings may reflect prompt serialization rather than user preference. items.title: The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems
items.abstract_600: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has recently emerged as a method to extend beyond the pre-trained knowledge of Large Language Models by augmenting the original prompt with relevant passages or documents retrieved by an Information Retrieval (IR) system. items.title: Large Language Models for Information Retrieval: A Survey
items.abstract_600: As a primary means of information acquisition, information retrieval (IR) systems, such as search engines, have integrated themselves into our daily lives. These systems also serve as components of dialogue, question-answering, and recommender systems. items.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
items.abstract_600: Rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in enterprise settings has introduced operational, security, and governance risks. As generative AI applications move from pilot to production, manual harm identification and mitigation are becoming difficult to scale. Although many tools support model evaluation, adversarial testing, runtime guardrails, and observability, the tooling landscape remains fragmented. items.abstract_600: This paper presents an agentic multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework for domain-specific literature reasoning, instantiated on a curated corpus of several thousand papers in intelligent tires, vehicle dynamics, vehicle control, sensing, estimation, and machine learning. items.title: Labeling Copilot: A Deep Research Agent for Automated Data Curation in Computer Vision
items.abstract_600: Curating high-quality datasets of images and annotations is a major bottleneck for deploying robust vision systems over vast, unlabeled data lakes. items.abstract_600: Deep research, in which an agent searches the open web, collects evidence, and derives an answer through extended reasoning, is a prominent use case for frontier language models. Frontier deep research products score high on existing benchmarks, making it difficult to distinguish their capabilities from current evaluation data alone. items.title: LitFM: A Retrieval Augmented Structure-aware Foundation Model For Citation Graphs
items.abstract_600: With the advent of large language models (LLMs), managing scientific literature via LLMs has become a promising direction of research. items.title: Ranked by Position: Order Sensitivity as an Exploitable Attack Surface in LLM Listwise Recommenders
items.abstract_600: Large language models (LLMs) used as listwise rerankers in recommendation systems suffer from position bias when serializing candidate sets into prompts. items.title: Lacuna: A Research Map for Machine Learning
items.abstract_600: Lacuna is a research map for machine learning that uses LLMs to turn papers and scholarly metadata into markdown summaries, concept elements, research directions, and research proposals. items.abstract_600: The exponential growth of scientific literature poses unprecedented challenges for researchers attempting to synthesize knowledge across rapidly evolving fields. We present \textbf{Agentic AutoSurvey}, a multi-agent framework for automated survey generation that addresses fundamental limitations in existing approaches. items.abstract_600: Most visual recognition studies rely heavily on crowd-labelled data in deep neural networks (DNNs) training, and they usually train a DNN for each single visual recognition task, leading to a laborious and time-consuming visual recognition paradigm. items.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
items.abstract_600: Chemistry literature synthesis often requires assembling specific findings scattered across many publications, yet existing literature-search systems primarily return ranked document lists. As a result, scientists and AI agents need to locate relevant information, verify their provenance, and assemble cross-paper answers manually. items.abstract_600: While large language models (LLMs) have shown impressive NLP capabilities, existing IR applications mainly focus on prompting LLMs to generate query expansions or generating permutations for listwise reranking.
